summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplantation, and recurrent urinary tract infections presented with malaise, lightheadedness, and malodorous urine. She was referred from her transplant clinic after a positive urine culture and low blood pressure. On admission, she was fluid-resuscitated for hypotension and started on oral cefpodoxime for a confirmed E. coli UTI, resistant to fluoroquinolones. Her acute kidney injury, likely due to dehydration, resolved with IV fluids. Blood glucose levels remained elevated but without ketosis, and she adjusted her insulin pump dosing accordingly. All home medications, including immunosuppressants, were continued. She improved clinically, with normalized vital signs and labs, and was discharged home on a 10-day course of antibiotics with follow-up planned through her transplant team.
